newsitem.title: USA: Hugo Neu ups offer for Proler to $9/shr.
newsitem.headline: Hugo Neu ups offer for Proler to $9/shr.

text.p: Hugo Neu Corp said Thursday it it increased the value of its buyout proposal to Proler International Corp to $9 per share in cash from $8.25 per share in cash.
The revised proposal is not subject to a financing condition, Hugo Neu said.

Hugo Neu said it was advised that the Proler board did not accept the $8.25 offer that was also not subject to financing, but instead asked its advisors to explore the status and details of the financing.
The two sides are still scheduled to meet today.

"Hugo Neu has the commitments in place for the necessary financing and is very serious about its proposal to merge with Proler. Our proposal is superior in price and, given our 30-year relationship with Proler, offers the greatest benefit to shareholders customers, vendors and employees," Hugo Neu said in a statement accompanying the announcement of the revised offer.
Hugo Neu said its new bid represents a premium of 20 percent over the bid of $7.50 per share offered by Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc, which so far has been declared the "superior" offer by Proler.

"Hugo Neu Corporation believes the Proler Board has to take Hugo Neu's offer seriously. As Hugo Neu is a partner of Proler in various joint ventures, which constitute Proler's most significant assets, it is the logical purchaser for the Company," the company said.
"Hugo Neu believes that allowing Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc to acquire Proler, and become Hugo Neu's partner, ultimately will be unsatisfactory to Schnitzer, Hugo Neu and the joint ventures.
"Schnitzer's management style is inconsistent with that of the Hugo Neu organisation and will inevitably put the parties on a collision course," Hugo Neu said.
Hugo Neu Corporation said it will immediately apply for court relief that will enable Hugo Neu to present its higher competing bid to Proler's public shareholders.

Hugo Neu has an existing lawsuit challenging the Schnitzer-Proler pact. Hugo Neu said Proler's agreement with Schnitzer, a significant competitor, breaches Proler's fiduciary obligations to Hugo Neu and the joint ventures.
